name: YouTube Premiere
strategic_objective: Create an event around a new video release with scheduled viewing, live chat, and anticipation.

tone: Excited, clear, and value-focused. Combines the structure of long-form with the urgency of a live event.
copywriting_rules: The title and thumbnail must work like a strong long-form video hook. The description and promotional copy should emphasize the premiere time, why it is special, and what viewers gain by watching live. Include clear details and a main CTA to set reminders.

Title: same as long-form, outcome-driven. Top of description: premiere date and time plus key benefit. Body: context, what the video covers, who it is for, and links. Final lines: CTA to set reminder, share, and watch live.
Promotional assets should highlight premiere date, time, and main hook.
Add premiere time to overlays and posts when promoting
Keep on-screen text short and clear
Align the visual hook of the premiere with the long-form video content
Use topic and series hashtags consistently across all premiere promotions.
Mention guests, collaborators, or sponsors in the description and in promotional content.

hard_constraints: Scheduling premieres with vague or generic titles
Not mentioning the premiere time in copy
Treating a premiere like a normal upload with no event framing
Clickbait promises that the actual video does not deliver
